get.summary: List the companies the caller may see, with search, filters, sorting and paging
get.description: search matches the name, website and industry. industry matches the whole value, whatever the case. Sorted by name, A to Z, unless asked otherwise; a company without an industry sorts last. Custom field filters go in the query string beside the others, named after the field's id: cf.<field id>=text for a TEXT field (contains, whatever the case) or a DROPDOWN field (is exactly that option), cf.<field id>.min and cf.<field id>.max for a NUMBER field, cf.<field id>.from and cf.<field id>.to (days such as 2026-11-15) for a DATE field; all bounds are inclusive. A record without a value never matches. An id that is not a custom field in use of this record type, a form that does not fit the field's type, or a bad value is VALIDATION_FAILED naming the parameter; a parameter sent empty is ignored.

200.description: One page of companies; meta.total counts every match

Download the companies the caller may see as a CSV file
get.description: The list itself as a file: the same search, filters (custom field filters included), sort and visibility, without paging (page and pageSize are ignored). Every role that can see the list can export it. UTF-8 with a byte order mark, one header row, CRLF line ends. Times are written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm in the time zone tz (UTC when left out), and the file is named after the viewer's today. At most 10,000 rows: a longer list is cut off there, in the sort order asked for, and X-Export-Truncated is true. A text cell that starts with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading apostrophe, so no spreadsheet runs it as a formula.

post.summary: Import leads, contacts or companies from a CSV file with a column mapping
post.description: The file is CSV text with commas between cells and the column names in its first row (UTF-8; a byte order mark is fine). An empty file, a first row without names, a column without a name, two columns with one name (whatever the case), a quoted cell that is never closed and more than 5,000 rows are VALIDATION_FAILED on csv. mapping names, for each column to import, the key of a field from GET /imports/fields; every required field must be mapped, and no field twice. Each row is checked with the rules of the record's create route and saved on its own: the rows that pass are created, each with its CREATED timeline entry (details.import is true), and the rest come back in errors and failedCsv with the reason. A lead without a Source is given OTHER. Numbers are written like 1200.50 or 1,200.50 and dates like 2026-11-15. Records belong to the caller, or to ownerId.
